items.title: LLM Judge Audit
items.description: Open-source tool that tests whether an LLM judge can be trusted before you rely on its scores: position bias, length bias, self-preference and repeat consistency against human labels. Across six open judges, raw accuracy ranked them wrong.
items.longDescription:
## About

Before you trust an LLM judge's scores, you should know how it fails. This tool audits a judge across four failure modes and reports the metrics that actually track agreement with human labels.

## What it measures

- **Position bias**: does the verdict change when the two answers swap places?
- **Length bias**: does padding a worse answer improve its score?
- **Self-preference**: does the judge favour text from its own model family?
- **Consistency**: is the verdict stable across repeated evaluations?
- **Baseline validity**: raw accuracy and Cohen's kappa against human labels

## Method

150 hard pairs from JudgeBench, same prompt, same seed, every judge self-hosted so the comparison is like for like.

## What it found across six open judges

- **Accuracy ranks judges wrong.** Ministral-8B beats Qwen3-4B on raw accuracy while scoring a kappa of 0.05, barely above chance agreement.
- **Scaling saturates.** Qwen3 14B and 32B are identical within noise.
- **Family beats size.** phi-4 at 14B judges worse than Qwen3-4B at a third the size.
- **The best judge is not the biggest.** gpt-oss-20b wins on the honest metrics.

items.title: KV Cache Optimization
items.description: Research on KV-cache compression for LLMs. Starts from a comparison of attention mechanisms (MHA / MQA / GQA / MLA) on toy models, then develops production-scale techniques (streaming recurrent state conversion and multi-tier adaptive compression) targeting Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Best configuration holds **0.38x memory at 8.05 perplexity against a 7.96 baseline**, measured on an H100.
items.longDescription:
## About

Research project exploring KV cache compression strategies for large language models. Starts from a comparison of attention mechanisms (MHA, MQA, GQA, MLA) on toy models, then develops and benchmarks production-scale techniques, including streaming recurrent state conversion and multi-tier adaptive compression, targeting Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.

## Project Structure

```
KV-cache-optimization/
├── AttentionHeads/           Toy 16M-param models comparing MHA / MQA / GQA / MLA
│   ├── mha/                  Multi-Head Attention (baseline)
│   ├── mqa/                  Multi-Query Attention
│   ├── gqa/                  Grouped Query Attention
│   ├── mla/                  Multi-Head Latent Attention (DeepSeek-V2 style)
│   ├── notebooks/            Training and evaluation notebooks
│   └── results/              Comparison plots and analysis
│
├── streaming_attention/      Per-head KV cache → recurrent state conversion
│   ├── head_classifier.py    DuoAttention pattern loading + head classification
│   ├── state_attention.py    Decayed linear state: S_t = λ·S_{t-1} + v_t·k_tᵀ
│   ├── hybrid_attention.py   Monkey-patches Llama for hybrid KV/state attention
│   ├── calibration.py        Two-stage tuning: per-head MSE + LoRA fine-tuning
│   ├── importance.py         Multi-signal token importance scoring
│   ├── adaptive_cache.py     Tiered KV cache (FP16 / INT8 / INT4 / evict)
│   ├── stratigraphic.py      Per-head zone assignment with geological metaphor
│   └── notebooks/            Experiments on H100 (zero-shot, calibration, benchmarks)
│
├── kv_bench/                 Benchmarking framework for KV cache strategies
│   ├── strategies/           8 strategy implementations
│   ├── runner.py             Model loading + strategy execution
│   └── report.py             Console / JSON / Markdown output
│
└── docs/                     Research diary and design documents
```

## Packages

**AttentionHeads**: foundational comparison of four attention architectures on TinyStories and SimpleStories. Each variant is a ~16M-parameter decoder-only transformer.

**streaming_attention**: production-scale KV cache optimization for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Streaming heads (identified by DuoAttention) are converted to fixed-size recurrent state matrices, while retrieval heads keep full or tiered KV cache. Includes a two-stage calibration pipeline (decay alignment + LoRA) and multi-tier adaptive compression.

**kv_bench**: unified benchmarking framework comparing 8 KV cache strategies: FullKV baseline, H2O, SnapKV, INT8 / INT4 uniform quantization, Stratigraphic compression, StreamingAttention, and Hybrid.

## Quick Start

```bash
pip install -e .                    # Install streaming_attention package
pip install -e ".[fla]"             # + Flash Linear Attention kernels
pip install -e ".[train]"           # + PEFT/Accelerate for calibration

# Run benchmarks
python -m kv_bench \
  --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --pattern-dir attn_patterns/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --strategies baseline streaming_attention h2o snapkv int8 int4 \
  --output results.json -v
```

## Key Results

| Strategy           | Perplexity | Memory vs Baseline |
|--------------------|-----------:|-------------------:|
| FullKV (baseline)  |       7.96 |              1.00× |
| H2O (50%)          |       8.31 |              0.50× |
| SnapKV (50%)       |       8.15 |              0.50× |
| INT8               |       7.97 |              0.50× |
| INT4               |       8.42 |              0.25× |
| Stratigraphic      |       8.05 |              0.38× |

## References

- [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) (Vaswani et al., 2017)
- [Fast Transformer Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02150) (Shazeer, 2019), MQA
- [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245) (Ainslie et al., 2023)
- [DuoAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10819) (Xiao et al., 2024), head classification
- [H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.14048) (Zhang et al., 2023)
- [SnapKV](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14469) (Li et al., 2024)

items.title: Git-RLMs
items.description: Framework that lets LLMs analyze git repositories through an iterative REPL loop, exploring code incrementally instead of loading entire codebases into context. **Twelve tools, sub-model delegation and hard cost budgets.**
items.longDescription:
## About

Git-RLMs is a framework that enables LLMs to explore and analyze git repositories through an iterative REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop). Instead of dumping an entire codebase into context, the model incrementally discovers relevant code using 12 built-in tools.

## How It Works

1. The LLM sends a tool command (e.g., `git_log`, `read_file`, `search_code`)
2. The REPL executes it against the repository
3. Results feed back to the LLM for the next exploration step
4. Sub-model delegation via `llm_query` for focused analysis

## Available Tools

`git_log`, `git_show`, `git_diff`, `search_code`, `read_file`, `list_files`, `get_file_at_commit`, `git_blame`, `git_branches`, `git_tags`, `llm_query`, `python_exec`

## Features

- CLI and Python API
- Supports OpenAI and Anthropic as LLM providers
- Cost tracking and trajectory logging for reproducibility
- Sandboxed Python execution environment

items.title: Fracture
items.description: Fuzzer that finds bugs in LLM serving systems by mutating their internal state directly, KV cache blocks, scheduler queues and prefix caches, rather than poking the API. Five real bugs filed against vLLM and SGLang.
items.longDescription:
## About

Most fuzzers test an inference engine through its API. Fracture goes underneath: it snapshots the engine's internal state, mutates it directly, and checks what breaks with a set of oracles.

## How it works

Three protocols: **Target** (the engine interface), **Mutator** (state perturbation) and **Oracle** (bug detection). Snapshots cover KV cache blocks, scheduler queues and prefix caches.

## Bugs found in production engines

- KV cache corruption from stale prefix reuse across scheduler steps (vLLM #38715)
- Block table aliasing when cache groups with different layouts share raw tensors (vLLM #41657)
- TOCTOU races where cache hits are evicted between scheduler phases (vLLM #42289)
- Radix cache boundary bugs producing nondeterministic output (SGLang #22819)
- Empty batch crashes from KV-pool retraction creating zero-length CUDA kernel launches (SGLang #24252)

items.title: Orbit Wars
items.description: Ongoing work on adversarial robustness for autonomous satellites: train a satellite to plan its own operations with reinforcement learning, feed it false sensor readings to break it, then build alarms that catch the lie.
items.longDescription:
## About

Satellites increasingly decide for themselves when to charge, take photos and send data home, and they decide from their sensor readings. So I trained one with PPO, fed it false readings to break it, then built alarms to catch the lie.

## Where it stands

The PPO pilot reaches **97% survival at a score of 38.5**, against **77% and 21.3** for a hand-written rule baseline.

Three detectors, measured against a 40 to 53% random-guess baseline:

- Geometry alarm catches a faked eclipse **100%** of the time, within 3 minutes
- A pattern model catches hidden ground stations **97%** of the time, within 34 minutes
- A power alarm catches battery overstatement **93%** of the time, within 3 hours

## Status

Active. The attack and detection results above are in the repo, along with a write-up of the mistakes made along the way.

items.title: Field Report
items.description: Finds how a Python library is actually used across GitHub, and where real usage diverges from the library's own documentation. Give it a package name and it does the rest.
items.longDescription:
## About

Documentation shows how a library is meant to be used. Field Report shows how it is used. Give it a package name and it finds dependent repositories, reads their call sites, and diffs real usage against the library's own examples.

## Pipeline

1. **Find**: query repositories that depend on the package
2. **Fetch**: clone them and verify the imports are real
3. **Read**: extract call sites from source
4. **Canon**: pull the examples from the library's own docs
5. **Compare**: diff real usage against documented usage
6. **Report**: emit Markdown, backed by SQLite

Runs in parallel on Modal, roughly 5 minutes against 15 sequential.

## Example finding

Across **119 repositories** using `clerk-backend-api`: one symbol imported through **5 different paths** in the wild, and **0 of 544 calls** use retries even though the library ships a `RetryConfig`.

items.title: ZeroToDiffusion
items.description: From-scratch implementation of diffusion models, worked end to end: probability review, KL divergence, ELBO, VAE, then DDPM, to understand image generation from first principles.
items.longDescription:
## About

I kept reading about Stable Diffusion and DALL-E but the math never clicked from blog posts alone. So I decided to go through it properly. Pen and paper first, then code.

## How I went about it

Week 1 was just probability: Gaussians, Bayes, KL divergence, ELBO. Boring but necessary. Turns out the entire loss function makes sense once you actually derive it yourself.

Then I built a VAE on MNIST. VAEs and diffusion models share the same probabilistic backbone, so this made the transition way smoother than jumping straight into DDPM.

After that: the forward process (gradually adding noise to images), the reverse process (learning to denoise), training a UNet to predict the noise, and finally generating images from pure noise. Seeing it work for the first time was honestly pretty satisfying.

## Takeaways

- The connection between VAEs and diffusion clicked once I saw both as learning to reverse a destruction process
- Noise schedules matter more than I expected for sample quality
- Attention layers are what give diffusion models their ability to capture global structure

## Papers I worked through

- Kingma & Welling (2014), VAEs
- Ho et al. (2020), DDPM

items.title: CrossGen
items.description: Cross-domain idea generator that solves problems by mapping structural relationships across unrelated fields using analogical reasoning, not surface-level keyword matching.
items.longDescription:
## About

CrossGen is a cross-domain idea generator that discovers solutions by mapping deep structural relationships across unrelated fields. Instead of asking "what field resembles mine," it identifies fundamental relational patterns that transcend surface features using Gentner's Structure-Mapping Theory.

## Pipeline

1. Decompose the problem into domain-neutral relations
2. Abstract through four parallel frameworks (SAPPhIRE, Biologize, WordTree, TRIZ)
3. Expand to 6-8 distant domains
4. Mine for structural analogies
5. Synthesize actionable solutions
6. Evaluate on novelty, feasibility, and depth

## Design choices

- Maps RELATIONS, not surface features
- Mandatory honesty: at least three specific weak spots per solution
- 40 universal principles and 42 curated domains across 8 categories
- Deterministic TRIZ lookups complemented by LLM reasoning to prevent hallucination
- CLI and web UI with live streaming output

items.title: Prompt Repetition Experiment
items.description: Research replication testing whether repeating a prompt inside one request improves small-model accuracy. Replicated across nine open models with McNemar significance testing, including the benchmarks where the effect did not survive.
items.longDescription:
## About

A research experiment investigating whether repeating prompts within a single request boosts accuracy on standardized benchmarks for small language models.

## Findings

- Tested 9 open-source models (0.5B to 9B parameters)
- Benchmarks: ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA, GSM8K, HellaSwag, NameIndex
- Significance tested with McNemar's test rather than raw accuracy deltas
- Largest effect on ARC-Challenge, 22% to 44% with triple repetition (p=0.022), reported alongside the benchmarks where the effect did not survive
- Works because the second copy of the prompt gets to attend to the first, giving the model a quasi-bidirectional pass

items.longDescription:
## About

An AI-powered lead generation tool designed for pharmaceutical sales teams. It discovers doctors and medical professionals across Algeria's 58 wilayas using the Google Maps Places API, then scores and deduplicates leads for export.

## Workflow

1. **Business context input**: Describe your product and target audience
2. **AI refinement**: DeepSeek generates clarifying questions to narrow the search
3. **Search matrix**: Combines wilayas with medical specialties for full coverage
4. **Lead deduplication**: Uses rapidfuzz fuzzy matching to merge duplicate entries
5. **Quality scoring**: AI-driven scoring of each lead's relevance
6. **Excel export**: Download clean, scored lead lists

## Tech Stack

- Streamlit wizard UI for step-by-step interaction
- Google Maps Places API for location-based discovery
- DeepSeek LLM for search refinement and scoring
- rapidfuzz for lead deduplication

## About

items.title: Mini Compiler
items.description: Lexical analyzer and parser for Mini3ADR, a small language with variables, arithmetic and control flow, built with Flex and Bison for a compiler construction course.
items.longDescription:
## About

A lexical analyzer and parser for Mini3ADR, a simple programming language designed for a compiler construction course. The project covers the front-end stages of compilation.

## Language Features (Mini3ADR)

- Integer variable declarations
- Assignment statements
- Arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /)
- Relational operators (<, >, ==, !=)
- Control flow: `while` loops and `if`/`else` statements

## Implementation

- **Lexer**: Tokenization with line tracking using Lex/Flex
- **Symbol table**: Tracks declared variables and their types
- **Parser**: `parser.y` grammar built with Yacc/Bison, wired up through a Makefile and compiled with GCC

items.title: Harry Potter Text Generator
items.description: Character-level text generator using vanilla RNNs trained on Harry Potter, exploring sequence modeling and the vanishing gradient problem in recurrent architectures.
items.longDescription:
## About

A character-level text generation project using Recurrent Neural Networks trained on the Harry Potter corpus. The goal was to understand sequence modeling from first principles and observe where vanilla RNNs break down.

## Technical Approach

- Character-level tokenization with one-hot encoding
- Vanilla RNN cells with tanh activation and hidden state propagation
- Cross-entropy loss with temperature-controlled softmax sampling
- Backpropagation through time (BPTT) with gradient clipping

## What I learned

- Vanishing gradients make it difficult for vanilla RNNs to capture long-range dependencies, the model loses coherence beyond short phrases
- Without gating mechanisms (LSTM/GRU), the hidden state saturates and forgets earlier context
- Temperature tuning is critical: too low produces repetitive text, too high produces gibberish
- This project motivated my subsequent LSTM from Scratch implementation to address these limitations
